label: Carpathian goat

links.name: Comparative Study on Production Efficiency in Native Romanian Carpatina and Banat White Goats (SPASB)

names.text: "Carpatina" is the name the 2017 Romanian study uses for the breed. The Wikipedia article gives "Carpathian goat" and the Carpathian label.

about.text: The Carpathian is a usually white-coated goat from southeastern Europe, kept in Romania and Poland. It is used for both meat and milk. Romanian studies describe it as a hardy, low-yielding breed, adapted to harsh conditions.

links.name: Comparative Study on Production Efficiency in Native Romanian Carpatina and Banat White Goats (SPASB)

sources.text: Wikipedia: a usually white-coated breed from southeastern Europe, countries Romania and Poland, used for meat and milk. The hardy, low-yielding character is from WebSearch excerpts of Romanian studies (the 2017 SPASB paper and a review it cites); the excerpts describe the breed as low-performing but well adapted.
Countries from the Wikipedia article. The article does not give a formation date.

sources.text: Fetched page: milk yield in Carpatina goats averaged 323.6 kg per lactation (SE 1.68), 2017 study at the Caransebes sheep and goat station. Earlier estimates of 240-260 kg and a review range of 220-350 kg per lactation were found only in WebSearch excerpts and are not used here. The number of does and the lactation length were not in the fetched text.
Wikipedia: used for the production of meat and milk.

gaps: Searched for: the formation or origin date (Wikipedia has none; the Oklahoma State breed page did not turn up in search); the current population and herd size (no DAD-IS record found); the FAO DAD-IS risk status (not found); lactation length per lactation (not in the fetched text); milk composition (not found); an Oklahoma State Breeds of Livestock entry (not found).
